name: Germany: participant-facing document QC
item_format: Each result records the item id, the outcome, a short rationale and evidence (quoted passage and source locator) or an explicit gap.

items.check: Protocol title, code, EU trial number, version and date match the current protocol.
Sponsor and site information are current and complete.
Investigational and comparator treatments are named and described as in the protocol and IB/SmPC.
Study purpose, phase and participant population match the protocol.
Randomisation ratio, treatment groups, placebo and blinding are explained correctly in plain language.
Visit schedule, duration, procedures, tests and follow-up match the schedule of activities.
Number and volume of samples match the protocol and sample plan.
Participant restrictions and prohibited treatments are stated.
Expected benefits and treatment alternatives are stated without overstating benefit.
Reimbursement, compensation, insurance and contacts are present and correct.
No statements carried over from another protocol, country, cohort or study phase.

sections.title: Protocol-to-participant-document consistency
sections.instruction: Compare line by line with the protocol, IB, risk section, pharmacy information, data-flow description, sample plan and insurance evidence.

items.check: Every research-only procedure is visible to the participant.
Risk frequency and severity are not softened compared with the IB/protocol.
Pregnancy testing and contraception periods match the protocol.
Treatment interruption and withdrawal rules match the protocol.
Optional procedures are not described as mandatory.
Planned remote visits, electronic consent, home nursing, wearables or direct-to-participant shipment are explained.
Insurance wording matches the certificate and policy terms (DE-O1, DE-O2).
Data and sample retention periods are consistent across all documents.
After a protocol change, every affected participant document has been reopened, not only the main adult form.
The main participation decision is separate from optional choices.
Express consent to processing personal and health data is present.
Optional future use, genetics, additional sampling, re-contact and pregnancy follow-up have separate choices where required.
Refusing an optional activity does not block main-study participation, unless scientifically necessary and justified in the application.
Withdrawal language explains the right to stop and the lawful limits on deleting data already collected.
The person signing has legal authority for the decision.
Participant and physician signature order and timing are clear (before any trial-specific procedure).
A signed copy is provided to the participant or representative.
Re-consent triggers are defined: new information, new versions, regained capacity, reaching adulthood.
The consent form does not introduce information absent from the information sheet.

sections.title: Population and document coverage
sections.instruction: Map every inclusion pathway in the protocol to an information and consent set (see requirements.json population_sets).

items.check: Every population that can enter the trial has its own information and consent set.
Healthy volunteers: states no therapeutic benefit, explains early-phase uncertainty, restrictions, payment, contraception and confinement accurately.
Minors: legal-representative consent, age- and maturity-appropriate information, the capable minor's own written consent, dissent, and re-consent at 18.
Adults without capacity: representative authority, adapted participant information, objection handling, capacity reassessment, and the German advance-consent condition for group-benefit research.
Emergency enrolment: every Article 35 condition, absence of known objection, investigator certification, later information and consent, right to object to use of data.
Participant unable to write: inability to sign is not confused with lack of capacity; alternative-recording method and impartial-witness block present.
Pregnancy follow-up: pregnant participant vs pregnant partner identified; record holders, infant data and whose consent is required are clear.
Secondary or future use is optional and has a separate information and consent document.
Controller and data-protection contact identified.
Categories of personal and health data listed; only special categories actually processed, each with a study-specific lay justification.
Each processing purpose explained.
Coding or pseudonymisation explained, and where the key is held.
Direct access by monitors, auditors, inspectors and authorities explained.
Recipients and transfers to sponsor, processors, authorities and regulatory applicants explained.
Safety reporting and CTIS reporting explained.
Transfers outside the EEA, safeguards or risks, and an explicit choice where the transfer is not essential.
Retention periods stated.
Participant rights and a practical contact route.
Withdrawal and the German rules allowing necessary continued processing.
Express written or electronic health-data consent with all disclosures under section 40b(6) AMG.
No promise of anonymity where coded data are used, and no promise of deletion that conflicts with safety, scientific-integrity or regulatory duties.
Sample type, volume, frequency and timing for every sample.
Protocol purpose and planned analyses.
Whether genetic testing is involved.
Coding, storage location, duration and responsible organisation.
Transfers and recipient categories.
Exhaustion, return or destruction.
Handling of incidental findings where applicable.
Whether commercial research is possible.
Withdrawal options and practical limits.
Protocol use clearly separated from optional use outside the protocol; separate optional document present where needed (AKEK).
Consistent with the S1 biological-samples form and the GDPR statement.
All participant and representative documents are in German.
Planned non-German enrolment has qualified translations and a communication plan.
The AKEK adult patient or healthy-volunteer model was used as baseline; every deviation from the model text is justified and visibly identifiable (AKEK guideline, 9 April 2026).
The physician-led information process matches section 40b(2) AMG.
Trial-participant insurance wording matches German coverage (min. EUR 500,000 per case of death or continuing incapacity).
Vulnerable-population pathways match sections 40b(3) to 40b(5) AMG.
The data section contains every disclosure in section 40b(6) AMG.
Recruitment material avoids promotional claims and undue emphasis on payment.
Endpoint-related patient-facing documents follow the Part I (English source) / Part II (German translation) route.
Radiation information and Part II documentation are included where the 2025 German radiation route applies.
Short summary of at most two pages, visually highlighted; Part I and Part II structure; risk frequencies use the four German categories.
Correct document title, population, language code, version and date.
Version references inside the consent form match the information sheet.
No participant, representative or physician signature in the blank CTIS submission copy.
Complete signature and date fields for use at consent.
Witness fields only where the alternative-signature pathway can apply.
Representative capacity or relationship field where relevant.
Page numbering; participant initials only if the process requires them.
Statement that the participant receives a signed copy.
Correct CTIS section and naming convention.
No personal data that should not appear in the CTIS upload.
No drafting instruction remains in the final version (italic notes, [bracket] notes, ........... gaps, yellow [EINFÜGEN/FALLS/AUSWAHL/HINWEIS] labels); fields completed by hand at consent stay blank.
The first pages answer what the trial is, what happens, the main risks and the alternatives.
Short sentences; medical terms explained at first use.
Risks grouped and prioritised.
Numbers, probabilities, visit counts and periods are easy to find.
Headings make the document easy to scan.
Optional choices look optional.
German terminology consistent and natural.
Translations reviewed by a qualified person and matching the approved source.
items.applies_when: document is adapted from a reference document in another language

items.check: Usable printed, on a phone and electronically.
The participant document list matches the protocol's population, country, site, procedure, data and sample matrices, and the Germany Part II package checklist.
